fields.meta_title: Yoga Landing Page Builder for Studios | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a yoga landing page that books classes up to the mat count, sorts teacher training applications, and counts retreat rooms.
fields.h1: Build a Yoga Landing Page That Books Classes by the Mat
fields.hero_description: Build a yoga landing page that books each class up to its mat count and saves every student to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Sits Behind a Yoga Studio's Page
fields.features_subheading: A student sees a schedule and a Book button. Behind them, six parts track which classes have room and who hears of a change.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt for the page and its bookings

Describe your classes and what a student should do next. Emergent builds the page and the table its bookings land in, then changes either one each time you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
A mat count on every class

Set how many mats each room holds, such as 18 for the main room. Each class on the page shows the mats left as students book, and a class that fills stops taking bookings.
fields.feature_3:
Emails when a class changes

Students get an email when a class they booked moves or is canceled. You change the class once by prompt, and the app writes to everyone booked into it with the new details.
fields.feature_4:
Bookings in a database you own

Every booking lands as a row in a database you own, with the class and the student who booked it. Send the rows to your email tool or CRM over its API so both lists match.
fields.feature_5:
Schedule changes by message

Tell Emergent that Sunday's restorative class now starts at 5:30 PM, or that a new teacher covers Fridays. The page changes at the same address, and past bookings stay in the table.
fields.feature_6:
Your studio's domain, your code

Put the page on your studio's custom domain, which is included and uses credits. On paid plans, export the page and its booking database to your GitHub repository and keep the code.

fields.usecase_heading: Yoga Landing Page Examples by Offer
fields.tab_content_1:
Bookings close on any class at 18 mats

Sunwick Yoga's schedule page caps every class at 18 mats, the number its main room holds. Students book with a name and an email, and the count on each class moves with every booking. Both 6:15 PM vinyasa classes this week reached 18 and show Full. Saturday's 9:00 AM slow flow has 5 mats left.
fields.tab_content_2:
Interviews go to applicants with 2 years or more

Ravelle Yoga School's 24-seat teacher training asks applicants for a name, an email, and years of practice, plus why they want to teach. Those with 2 or more years go on director Delphine Rourke's interview list. The rest get an email about the foundations series. Of 31 applications, 22 went to the list and 9 got the email.
fields.tab_content_3:
Private rooms and shared rooms each keep a count

For its 4-day lake retreat, Juniper Bend Yoga holds 20 spots: 12 in shared rooms and 8 in private rooms. A guest picks a room type and leaves a name and an email to request a spot. Each room type counts down on its own. With 15 requests in, 10 shared and 5 private, the page shows 2 shared and 3 private spots left.
fields.tab_content_4:
38 RSVPs heard by email when rain moved class indoors

Oakmere Yoga Collective teaches a free Sunday class in the park, and students RSVP with their name and email. Last Sunday, rain was forecast with 38 RSVPs in. Teacher Odette Marchetti changed the location by prompt, and the app emailed all 38 with the studio address and the same 9:30 AM start.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Yoga Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a yoga landing page around one offer and a real mat count, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one offer for the page
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Count the mats before you set a cap
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what the booking needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: A drop-in schedule and a weekend retreat ask different things of a visitor. Give each its own page, and decide the one action it asks for, such as booking a mat on Tuesday night or requesting a private room.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Lay out mats in each room at the spacing you teach with, then count them. Use that number as the class cap. Set a lower cap for classes that need more floor per student, such as restorative classes with bolsters and blankets.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List each class with its time and teacher, plus the mats left. A student who opens the page on a phone should see the next class to book without scrolling past a long welcome.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A drop-in class needs a name and an email. A teacher training also needs years of practice and a short answer on why the applicant wants to teach. A retreat adds a room type. Save longer questions for the first class or the interview.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put the cancel rule by the button
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write how late a student can cancel and what happens to the booking, in one sentence under the Book button. Put it where a student reads it before booking, not only in the confirmation email that arrives afterward.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Name who reviews training applications, who replies to retreat questions, and who covers the Sunday class when its teacher is away. Agree on how soon a request gets a reply, and write down the backup's name before the page goes live.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Each Monday, put last week's bookings next to the students who came in. A class that books out but has empty mats on the day may need a reminder email the evening before, or an earlier cancel deadline.

faq_plan.q: What is a yoga landing page?
faq_plan.a: A yoga landing page is a single web page built around one yoga offer, such as a class schedule or a retreat. It asks the visitor for one action, like booking a mat or sending an application, and leaves out the rest of the studio's site so nothing competes with that action.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a yoga landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the offer to Emergent's AI landing page builder: the classes or the program, what a student should do, and who should hear about each request. Emergent builds the page with a booking database you own, and you change any part by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a yoga studio landing page include?
faq_plan.a: The week's classes with their times and mats left, plus a Book button on each class. Add the studio's address, what a first-timer should bring, and the price of a drop-in class. Use a photo of the actual room, not a stock image.

faq_plan.q: How is a yoga landing page different from a gym page?
faq_plan.a: It sells classes with a fixed number of mats, not open floor time. The schedule and the spots left carry the page. A fitness landing page for a gym can lead with membership and equipment instead. If your studio also runs strength classes, give those their own page so each ad lands on one offer.

faq_plan.q: Should a yoga landing page show how many spots are left in each class?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when classes have a fixed mat count. A line such as 5 mats left tells a student to book now or pick another time, and a full class can link to the next one with room. The app Emergent builds can show those counts live as bookings arrive.

faq_plan.q: What should a yoga landing page for teacher training ask applicants?
faq_plan.a: Ask only what decides who gets an interview: contact details, how long the applicant has practiced, and why they want to teach. Put the dates, the total hours, and the full cost on the page itself. Applicants then know them before they apply.

faq_plan.q: Can a yoga landing page book private one-on-one sessions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A private teacher's page lists session lengths and prices, where sessions happen, and open times to request. It works much like a personal trainer landing page, with the style of practice in place of training goals. Ask each student about experience level before the first session, and plan it from the answer.

faq_plan.q: What should a yoga retreat landing page show before someone requests a spot?
faq_plan.a: The dates, the place, each room type with its spots left, and the full price per room type. Add what the price covers, such as meals and classes, and the cancellation terms. Put all of it above the request form, where a guest reads it before choosing a room.

faq_plan.q: Should a yoga landing page list drop-in and class pack prices?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the drop-in price and each class pack next to the schedule. A student then knows the cost before booking a mat. Keep the numbers the same as at the front desk. When a price changes, tell Emergent once and it changes the page at the same address, with every past booking kept in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a yoga landing page sell corporate classes to companies?
faq_plan.a: Yes, on its own page. Show the group sizes you teach and the price per session. That page reads closer to a consulting landing page than a class schedule. Ask for the company and the team size, then send each inquiry to one person.

plan.angle: Searches for a yoga landing page turn up template galleries and studio marketing tips: a hero photo, a class list and a contact form. None of them shows what the page does once a student acts: a class that stops at its mat count, a teacher training application sorted by years of practice, retreat rooms counted by type, a park class whose RSVPs hear about a move indoors. This page defines the term up top, then shows four working yoga pages by offer, each with the rule and the table behind it, and a how-to built on studio operating advice rather than design tips.
